=== FINDING 3 (CONFIRMED, PRE-EXISTING in main's scripts/lwb_lanes.py, NOT charged to this PR, but it decides what any reviewer can achieve here) ===
Same defect I recorded on PR #29. In `_review_ok`, the verdict test (line 646) runs BEFORE the staleness test (line 660) and APPENDS to `errors` rather than declining to count the record. So reviews/30/cloud-reviewer-b.json — which reviewed 1a171c9a, a head that is three commits stale, and whose two blocking findings are now FIXED — fails `lwb-lanes` permanently, and so will this record. A stale AGREE at the same position would be correctly skipped as stale; only a stale DISAGREE is eternal. The only mechanical route to green is to delete another reviewer's adverse record, which reviews/README.md calls falsifying evidence. The fix belongs in lwb_lanes.py, in its own PR: skip a record whose reviewed_commit is not the reviewable head BEFORE consulting its verdict, for every verdict alike.

=== FINDING 4 (NEW, CONFIRMED, and structural for the whole cloud loop) — the self-review collision rule produces a FALSE POSITIVE on this exact pair of identities, so the reviewer routine as specified CANNOT produce a gate-satisfying record for this author ===
My dispatching routine mandates the reviewer_id string "reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft". proof/30.json's `author` is "conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19". Both legitimately embed the repository's own name.
    $ python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import lwb_lanes as L; print(L._shared_long_segment('reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft-015LQaR6wLFe234ZtMdHtenC-2026-09-19','conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19'))"
    buildcraft
"buildcraft" is 10 characters, over MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH (8), so lwb_lanes rejects the pair as an accidental self-review. It is not one: these are two different sessions, one of which was dispatched by a cron entry the other cannot create.
This is precisely the false-positive class reviews/README.md names as the reason the floor sits at 8 — "the failure mode that gets a gate disabled" — and it is not hypothetical any more: it falls out of the routine-mandated reviewer id meeting the conductor's own author id, in the ordinary case. HAD I VOTED AGREE, THIS RECORD WOULD STILL HAVE BEEN REJECTED. That means the cloud reviewer routine, as currently specified, cannot satisfy the gate for any author whose id contains the repository name.
I did NOT mangle my identifier to dodge this. I kept the routine's mandated string verbatim as the role-and-model portion and appended my true session token and today's date, and I am reporting the collision instead of engineering around it — relabelling an identifier to make a gate pass is the thing there is a decision on the books about. The fix is not to rename anyone: it is for MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH's comparison to ignore a stop-list of non-identifying segments (the repo name, the org name), or for the routine specs to stop embedding the repository name in an identity string, decided deliberately and recorded.
